comparison.cause_isolation: Target, initial adaptive window estimate, and ceiling changed together; changes are descriptive, not a controlled performance effect.

findings: Both offered deficits reconcile to clipped pacing credit plus inferred boundary balance change with complete six-worker boundary samples; this is not quantum rounding or the 59-second canonical denominator.
Raising the configured adaptive ceiling did not bind either run: zero cap-limited ACKs; actual window peaked at16599/32301 and ended16340/16818 respectively.

The larger-window run has 224805.695 clipped measured tokens and68.409 measured client-hold worker-seconds, versus178522.129 and58.414. Client waits cover19.0024% versus16.2260% of six-worker measured exposure.

All observed code651 outcomes in both full runs are snapshot_changed. The not_ready parent-attempt rate rises8.1454%→14.4879%; mean batch residence64.830→104.705ms and mean changed-snapshot age95.729→155.318ms also rise. These are full-run wall timings, not measured verifier CPU.

A shared pressure episode is visible near elapsed110–130s, before timeout-driven AIMD decrease. In window64k, timeouts18 occur around122–125s while the sampled window falls32301→15463; post-episode issuance returns to approximately57.7–58.8k despite the smaller window. Therefore preventing window decrease alone is not established as a solution.

Generator CPU remains below one core on average; genesis mean CPU stays near9.4cores across the episode. Host CPU is already near75% and mean I/O wait around1.6–1.7%, without a matching sharp increase. No generator CPU saturation or single long >100ms token-update gap was observed.

The active NVMe devices show longer weighted I/O queues during the window64k episode (~3.13–3.14) than after it (~1.43–1.47), but write throughput is lower than before. This is compatible with I/O contention and does not identify compaction, flushing, or any specific periodic task.

Actor samples near113/114 and143/145 miss the122–125s timeout cluster. Thread capture is empty and the scheduling log has zero bytes. No actor-specific or periodic-work cause can be assigned from these captures.

recommended_next_calibration.decision: Use one predeclared180-second same-config calibration before changing window policy.
recommended_next_calibration.only_change_from_window64k: NATIVE_LOAD_DURATION_SECONDS:60→180; retain target60000, initial RTT0.5, adaptive max65536, batching64/coalesce20ms and all other existing settings.
recommended_next_calibration.rationale: The ceiling never bound, and the bottleneck precedes the AIMD collapse. A longer complete measurement retains the original pressure episode and tests whether it recurs; it avoids attributing a mixed change to a new fixed window. The already observed recovery segments sustain rates above the unchanged57000 ingress threshold.

quantitative_screen.qualification: Conditional arithmetic, not a prediction or capacity claim. Recurrent pressure or changing canonical rate can still reject the calibration.

recommended_next_calibration.acceptance: Require offered_avg>=57000 and actual offered_avg>canonical_avg, plus unchanged proof/completion/quantum/lane/cleanup/strict-reuse/observer gates. Save the entire180s window and all rejected results; do not choose favorable subsections. Repeat matched measurements before promotion.

headroom_estimate.scope: Arithmetic screen assuming the observed canonical rate persists; per-source limits and actual drain remain authoritative.

recommended_next_calibration.fixed_window_status: Deferred: disabling adaptive mode ties client capacity to the hard active-task limit in existing code. It would change the active-work queue as well as loss response and could raise snapshot/timeout pressure; the observed episode does not yet justify calling it an improvement.

source_evidence.claim: Initial adaptive window uses target*initial_RTT, clipped by cap; nonadaptive uses the hard client limit.
Eligible timeout/loss signals halve a client window at most once per100ms; snapshot/revision races are exempt through the policy helper.
Timeouts remain congestion signals while narrowly recognized snapshot/revision races do not decrease AIMD.

limitations: Both runs fail unchanged acceptance gates; no capacity improvement or winning configuration is established.

Only two sequential mixed-configuration observations exist. CPU/host/I/O summaries are sampled; device deltas use the first and last available samples inside each interval and cannot attribute writes to a process or operation.
Worker report snapshots are asynchronous. Segment rates normalize summed worker offer counts by mean worker measured exposure and are descriptive, not synchronized instantaneous TPS.

Server diagnostic deltas include ramp/warmup/drain; maxima are validator-lifetime before/after observations. Pacing/window telemetry alone cannot assign each clipped token to a particular retry or server wait.
The proposed longer run is a falsifiable calibration, not a relaxation of target/gates or a guarantee that the late recovery continues.
